historical_references.reference: Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism, was born as Har Gobind Khatri in the village of Talwandi in 1469. He was later given the name Guru Nanak Dev Ji by a Muslim Saint, Mardana, who became his closest companion and disciple. This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Guru', meaning teacher, and 'Nanak', meaning 'revealer of the hidden truth'.

Another figure in Hinduism named Guru was Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, the ninth Sikh Guru who lived from 1621 to 1675. He was known as 'Guru of Martyrs' as he sacrificed his life to prevent the invasion of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in 1675. The word 'Guru' in this context refers to a spiritual guide and teacher.
